summary: Orion is a browser-based astronaut health-monitoring prototype for long-duration space missions. It lets a crew member manually log health indicators, daily mood and stress check-ins, sleep, radiation exposure, and cabin conditions. The dashboard organizes entries into trend charts and a date-based journal, while example threshold flags explain why a reading may need review. A Mission Guide connects measurements to NASA’s human-spaceflight hazard categories. Orion aims to make observations easier to record and review in one place, including when no connected sensor is available. The prototype starts with simulated sample values and saves entries locally in the browser. It does not connect to sensors or NASA datasets, diagnose conditions, or provide validated medical or flight guidance.
details:
Orion is a self-contained browser prototype for organizing astronaut health and wellbeing observations. Users can manually enter measurements, complete daily mood, stress, and sleep check-ins, review a date-grouped journal and trends, and read explanations for example threshold flags. The Mission Guide provides spaceflight context and explains the limits of the measurements.

The project’s intended benefit is to make it easier to record and review different observations in one place, including without connected hardware. It is a demonstration, not a medical or operational tool: sample values are simulated, manual entries stay in the current browser, and there are no connected sensors or live NASA data feeds. Its thresholds are illustrative and are not validated medical standards.

The website was built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, using browser local storage. OpenAI Codex assisted with application code, interface text, documentation, and demo-slide text. The team should review and understand the final work.
